requiredChanges.title: The deep $ref `#/$defs/Ref/properties/domain` breaks the owning resolvers, including core admission
requiredChanges.why: This document has an implicit invariant the proposal is the first to break: every $ref is `#/$defs/<Name>` and the owning code resolves refs by `ref.split('/')[-1]`. Three sites: identity-model.py:589 `deref` (the admission walk calls deref at every node); identity-model.py:605 `carries_digest`; check-identity.py:887 `sort_canonical_sets` (reached through `rekey`, used by the stage fixture at check-identity.py:1519). All three do `SCHEMA['$defs']['domain']` and raise KeyError. identity-model.py:588 already refuses any ref that is not `#/$defs/`-prefixed with `EXTERNAL_SCHEMA_REF`, which shows the flat shape is an assumed contract, not an accident.

This is the systemically better fix — `split('/')[-1]` is a latent defect regardless of this proposal — but it edits identity-model.py and check-identity.py, i.e. three files, which is outside this proposal's stated two-file scope and touches the checker owner's surface. recommendedChanges.title: The operation paragraph states the ownership law but not its one concrete consequence
recommendedChanges.finding: The paragraph correctly and completely assigns the owner and forbids host respelling, but leaves the reader with no way to see why a shared token matters. The concrete mechanism, verified against $defs/cache-key: a cache or regeneration key is {planId, producerClosure, stageSpecDigest, scopeIds, inputRefs, outputSchemaDigest}, and stageSpecDigest covers operation + parameters + outputSchemaDigest. So RESPELLING is safe-by-construction (it changes stageSpecDigest, splitting the key — a miss, never a false reuse), while ONE TOKEN FOR TWO DISTINCT LOGICAL OPERATIONS of the same interface with the same parameters and output schema collapses two stages onto one key. That is the actual hazard the provider-authoring law exists to prevent, and it is unenforceable at the host boundary.
recommendedChanges.insertedInOverlay: 8 lines after 'The selected closure retains the implementation of that interface.' No new mechanism, no registry, no manifest member, no refusal code.

recommendedChanges.title: 'there is no platform-wide operation enum' reads against md:1069
recommendedChanges.finding: md:1069 says `operation` 'is one of the seven evaluator predicates' (program-predicate.operation, a real closed enum in this same document). 43 lines later the new paragraph says flatly 'there is no platform-wide operation enum'. The new paragraph is scoped by its opening `stage-spec.operation`, so it is not wrong; but a NEW blind consumer reading forward sees an unqualified contradiction of a sentence it just read. No behaviour is at risk (the enum is schema-enforced at program-predicate either way).
recommendedChanges.overlayText: 'there is no platform-wide enum of stage operations, unlike `program-predicate.operation`, whose seven evaluator predicates are closed.'

recommendedChanges.title: closureMembership.selectedThroughOtherInput import strings invert the law
recommendedChanges.finding: As written: 'plan.importIds; evaluated imports additionally require evaluationInputRefs membership.' Membership in proof.evaluationInputRefs is what DEFINES an evaluated import (identity-model.py:1427 derives the set from it); it is not an additional obligation on the import. The actual law at :1428 is the converse: an import named by evaluationInputRefs must be a plan.importIds member, refusing UNSELECTED_EVALUATION_IMPORT.

qualificationsOfTheRetainedAssessment.standing: These qualify the earlier bounded assessment's language. They are not defects in this proposal, which imports none of them.

runIdStability.qualification: No universal RunId stability follows from editing raw schema-document bytes, and none is claimed here. The correct statement is conditional and I verified both halves. (a) FOR THIS PROPOSAL, no record re-mints: identity-schemas.v2.json is loaded as the validator and registry (identity-model.py:6) and is NOT among the six documents whose bytes the payload registry digests, so its bytes are not a hashed input to any record in this bundle. (b) IN GENERAL the warning is right: any document that IS a registered artifact — the six payload-registry documents, and every registered parameter schema and stage output schema reached through the `raw-artifact` representation — re-mints `schemaDigest` / `outputSchemaDigest` on any byte edit, and therefore re-mints every complete record that selects it, with no change to any hash recipe. A recipe-stability argument is not an identity-stability argument.

publicRoute.qualification: The retained assessment's full-origin-independent public route was overbroad. Ownership, origin and event position still govern public failure. This proposal proposes no new universal route and no new public refusal: it adds zero code and zero refusal names. What it changes is which inputs reach a PRE-EXISTING schema-admission outcome — the same jsonschema ValidationError class that already refuses `operation=''` in frozen19 and that check-identity.py:19/29 already treat as an admission result. I make no claim about how that projects publicly; that is application review's.

c2Status.qualification: C2 historical status alone is not a complete current-authority grade, and the retained assessment's DO-NOT-SEAL / unresolved-REJECT note is a reason not to BIND to that artifact, not a grade of it. The point is moot here: this proposal imports no C2 vocabulary. The single `c2-plan-stage-schema.v4.json` mention in the md is pre-existing at line 62 and byte-identical to frozen19. All broad governance grading is left to application review.

aliasProbes.qualification: The original same-closure alias probes were closure-only. Different stage-spec inputs minting different RunIds is the identity function behaving correctly, not proved nondeterminism, and I did not use them as evidence for or against any choice here.
